This can feel dismissive or controlling, especially if others had different ideas for the night. 2. **Pompous behavior** – The word "pompous" suggests Jim may have acted superiorly, as if his choices were inherently better than anyone else’s. This can make people feel unheard or excluded. 3. **Group dynamics matter** – Game nights (or any shared activity) often thrive on collaboration or at least mutual respect. A better approach would be to: - Ask, "What games does everyone want to play?" - Compromise (e.g., "Let’s do two rounds of each"). - Or take turns picking games.
